raw_response:
My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for three generations. I have about 10 mu. There is no question what I grow — winter wheat, then summer maize. That is what this land is for. I have done this rotation every year for forty years. My neighbors do the same. The soil knows it. I know it.

For wheat, I will plant in mid-October, after the last heat passes. I buy Jimai seeds from the village cooperative — not the old seeds I save myself anymore, because those gave lower yield the last few years. The cooperative also sells the compound fertilizer I use. I apply it all at planting, plus some urea when the wheat greens up in spring. I know some people say you can use less, but my father always said the land needs to be fed. I irrigate before winter sets in, again at green-up, at jointing, and at heading. Four times. That is what the wheat needs here.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant maize immediately. I use hybrid seeds — everyone does now, you cannot buy anything else really. I apply fertilizer at planting and again when the maize is knee-high. I only irrigate once or twice for maize because the summer rains help. I spray for aphids and corn borer, usually twice.

I do rotary tillage before wheat. For maize I sometimes just seed into the stubble but usually do a light till.

I am 65. My back is not what it was. I will do what I can manage. My son helps during harvest.
